newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks post gains on baht stability, results.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks post gains on baht stability, results.

text.p: Thai stocks posted mild gains on Friday as a return of currency stability encouraged foreign investors to buy discounted stocks on a busy day full of corporate result releases, traders said.
The SET Index gained 3.32 points, or 0.60 percent, to end at 561.19. The SET 50 gained 0.26 points, or 0.64 percent, to 40.66. Turnover was 4.68 billion baht.

"The foreigners are coming in picking up cheap stocks. Once it became clear that the baht is not going to be devalued, at least during this current round, on valuations there are cheap stocks here," said foreign trader.
Corporate results were generally viewed by analysts as miserable but a decline in earnings had been widely anticipated and most results came in above worst case forecasts, they said.
"They were almost all poor, very poor, but predictably so," said an analyst at a leading European broker.

Communications stocks, hit in the morning by poor results from mobile operator United Communications Plc which posted a 42 percent decrease in profits, recovered in the afternoon as rival Advanced Info Services, which reported rising profits on Thursday, gained 14 to 175.
Energy stocks gained 3.11 percent after reporting broad gains in earnings and are benefitting as defensive buys, traders said.

The banks, which reported last month, edged higher though sales of Bangkok Bank Plc down three baht to 147, Thai Farmers Bank Plc off 0.50 to 97.50, and Siam Commercial Bank Plc which fell three to 117 continued as foreign holders sold as prices sank to year lows, traders said.
Finance stocks, which gained 2.42 percent, were bolstered by news of five billion baht central bank fund to help alleviate problem margin loans.
